entries.title: Psalms 46:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Though - Though there should be nothing but confusion, and desolations round about us: which are often expressed by such metaphors.

entries.title: Psalms 46:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: A river - This may design the gracious presence, and blessing of the Lord, which is frequently described under the name of waters. Make glad - Shall not barely preserve it from danger, but give great occasion for rejoicing and thanksgiving. The city - Jerusalem, the place where God's holy tabernacle is settled.

entries.title: Psalms 46:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Raged - Against God, and against his people. Uttered - He spake to them in his wrath. The earth - The inhabitants of the earth were consumed.

entries.title: Psalms 46:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Desolations - Among those who were vexatious to God's people.

entries.title: Psalms 46:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: To cease - He hath settled as in a firm and well - grounded peace. The land - Of Israel: from one end of it to the other. The bow - The bows and spears, and chariots of their enemies.

entries.title: Psalms 46:11–47:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Be still - Stir no more against my people. God - The only true and almighty God; your gods are but dumb and impotent idols. Exalted - I will make myself glorious by my great and wonderful works.
